{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"7e4ca785494855c730996591e9036a5e4d614709128da4e697d80448abe9a418","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:77","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Drugs, stopping, crashes and railroad crossings (crash duties, railroads and confusables)","heading":"C2 — Crash duties, railroad crossings and confusables","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Crash duties, railroad crossings and confusables

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A40
At a crash, collect the names and addresses of everyone involved and of any witnesses, and note other relevant details. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A40
If another person involved asks, give the name and address of your liability insurance company and your local agent, and if you cannot do so at the scene, provide it later. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A40
If you hit an unattended vehicle, either notify the police, try to find its owner, or leave a written note with your name and address where it will easily be seen on that vehicle. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A40
When a mishap damages any other kind of property, you must let the property owner know. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A40
A witness reporting a crash should give the exact location, whether the road is blocked, and the likely damage and injuries, and every crash should go to the law enforcement agency with jurisdiction. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A40
The round railroad warning sign is yellow with a black X and the letters RR, and it stands 750 feet before the track to warn of a crossing ahead. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A40
Before a crossing the pavement may carry a large X with two R's, a yellow line ahead of it means no passing, and white lines beside the track mark where to stop for a train. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A41
When crossing lights start flashing you must always stop and wait until it is safe to go. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F40 | anchor: A41
Red flashing lights warn you to stop as crossing gates come down, and you stay stopped until the gates rise and the lights quit flashing. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F41 | anchor: A41
At a crossing with no warning device, slow down and look and listen for trains before going on. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F42 | anchor: A41
The crossbuck sign appears at most crossings and means slow down and be ready to stop when a train is seen; a sign under it shows the number of tracks when there is more than one. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F43 | anchor: A41
School buses, church buses, all passenger buses, and trucks hauling flammables, explosives or other hazardous material must stop before every railroad crossing. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F44 | anchor: A41
The manual says a stop at a railroad crossing must be made within 15 to 50 ft of it. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F45 | anchor: A41
Approach slowly enough to be sure you can stop once a train first comes into view, and come to a complete stop at crossings protected by electric or mechanical signals as the manual directs. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F46 | anchor: A41
You must stop when the crossing gate is down or a train is approaching, and with more than one track you must be sure every track is clear before crossing [A41] [A42].
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F47 | anchor: A42
Never change gears while on the tracks, because that can stall the car; with a manual transmission, shift down before you cross. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F48 | anchor: A42
Expect a train on any track at any hour, and in heavy traffic do not start across until you know you can clear the crossing. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F49 | anchor: A42
After the last car of a train passes, wait until you are sure no second train is coming on another track, especially from the opposite direction. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F50 | anchor: A42
Driving around lowered gates is against the law, so stay put until they rise, and never race a train to the crossing. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F51 | anchor: A42
Be ready to stop when you follow buses or trucks that are required to stop at crossings. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F52 | anchor: A42
The manual reports that Alabama ranks #13 nationally for highway-railroad crossing deaths and that a crash with a train makes a motorist 40 times more likely to die. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F53 | anchor: A42
Crossing crashes kill more people in the United States each year than all aviation crashes together, and nearly 50% of train-vehicle collisions happen at crossings with active warning devices. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F54 | anchor: A42
Walking or playing on tracks, trestles, rail yards or equipment is illegal, and you should cross tracks only at designated crossings. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F55 | anchor: A42
If your vehicle stalls on a crossing, get everyone out right away and clear of the tracks, then call local law enforcement for help. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F56 | anchor: A42
Trains cannot stop quickly: a freight train going 55 mph needs a mile or more, about the length of 18 football fields. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A38
The two-second count is for good conditions, while bad roads, bad weather or a long vehicle call for four or five seconds. [A38]
Why it matters: group_hint following-distance; prereq_hint sec07-F10; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F13, sec07-F14.
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A40
A crash with injury or death is reported to police right away, while the written SR-31 within 30 days applies when an uninsured at-fault party is involved. [A40]
Why it matters: group_hint crash-reporting; prereq_hint sec07-F28; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec07-F29, sec07-F30.
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A40
The advance railroad sign is round and yellow and stands 750 feet before the track, while the crossbuck stands at the crossing itself. [A40]
Why it matters: group_hint railroad-signs; prereq_hint sec07-F37; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F37, sec07-F42.
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A41
Buses and hazardous-material trucks must always stop at crossings, while other drivers must stop for flashing lights, lowered gates or an approaching train. [A41]
Why it matters: group_hint railroad-stops; prereq_hint sec07-F39; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec07-F43, sec07-F46.
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A37
Antihistamines may cause drowsiness and confusion as side effects, while barbiturates produce drunk-like symptoms when used to excess. [A37]
Why it matters: group_hint drug-effects; prereq_hint sec07-F01; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec07-F04, sec07-F05.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0037]
